CPS mom Sher’Ron Hinton in her home in Monteclare on the Northwest Side in 2025. Chicago Public Schools records show that her daughter was the subject of incessant bullying, and the adults at her elementary school struggled and failed to extinguish it.

Zubaer Khan/Sun-Times

Share

The mother of a Black student who endured racist bullying for more than two years at a predominantly white Northwest Side elementary school is set to receive a $300,000 settlement from Chicago Public Schools.

The city’s Board of Education unanimously voted to approve the payment at its monthly meeting Thursday, more than a year after the Chicago Sun-Times and WBEZ published an investigation into the incessant bullying and failures by the school administration to curb it.

The student’s mother, Sher’Ron Hinton, filed a lawsuit against the district in July 2025 accusing the staff at Wildwood IB World Magnet School of “willful and wanton conduct” and negligence for allowing her daughter to be subjected to “extreme acts of race-based bullying, sexual harassment and sexual abuse.”

Hundreds of pages of school incident reports filled out by Wildwood staff and emails from educators showed the girl, who the Sun-Times and WBEZ called Jada to protect her identity, was subjected to repeated racial slurs, body-shaming, encouragement to kill herself and, in one case, touching “in places I don’t want to be touched.”

She told school employees four times in fifth grade that she had suicidal thoughts.

A Nov. 19, 2024 Wildwood School incident report about Jada provided to her mother by the school.

Hinton said reading through the incident reports was devastating.

“So when I got the documents, I asked (Jada), ‘Did this happen? Did this person do this to you?’ ” Hinton said in an interview in the spring of 2025. “And she told me that everything that was reported in her incident reports up until this year, 7th grade, happened. So it’s just like, ‘How do we get justice?’”

Hinton became aware of the severe problems after her daughter came home in October 2024 and told her a student called her the n-word. The district’s Office of Student Protection substantiated that Jada was the victim of racial bullying and the students were given in-school suspensions.

In this Dec 4, 2024 “urgent request” for all 7th grade teachers sent by the director of social-emotional learning at Wildwood Elementary School, the director lists a set of protocols they should all follow to support Jada “to ensure she is safe in every single one of her classes.” The director said Jada “is feeling targeted,” that she reported that day that another student was “verbally harassing her” and that “she feels unsafe in class or in any space at Wildwood.”

The experience left Jada in extreme emotional distress and she took time off school in the spring for intensive mental health treatment, her mother said. Hinton, who had been excited for her children to go to Wildwood, transferred Jada and her four siblings out of the school after classes ended in June 2025.

Hinton declined comment Thursday.

CPS officials didn’t immediately comment on the settlement.

In 2025, CPS officials defended the Wildwood administration’s handling of “incidents involving middle school students, including one student in particular.”

“In line with District policy, school leadership has consistently monitored and supported the students involved over the past two years,” a spokeswoman said in a written statement, noting that even complete school documents don’t capture everything about a school’s efforts or its communications with a family.

Some parents whose children were accused by Jada said their kids told them they were being falsely accused.

Kohen Wiley’s family pushes for federal investigation after baby’s shooting deemed justified

The family of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley is pushing to have the Department of Justice open an investigation into his death.

Actual Article Body:
SENATOBIA, Miss. (WMC/Gray News) - The family of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley is pushing to have the Department of Justice open an investigation into his death.

Kohen was shot and killed by a Senatobia police officer back on June 14 at the Senatobia Walmart parking lot.

Earlier this week, Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch’s office announced the officer was justified in his actions.

The Wiley family is represented by civil rights attorneys Ben Crump and Van Turner. The two held a press conference alongside the Wiley family and community activists Thursday morning.

“I’m having a difficult time understanding the word justified. I just don’t understand,” said LaSandra Williams, Kohen’s paternal grandmother.

Williams and Kohen’s maternal grandmother, Veronica Roberson, say they remain heartbroken.

According to Crump’s team, the Wiley family was able to review all of the surveillance and body camera footage from the shooting provided by the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation Thursday morning.

“Disgusted me. First, I want to say, the word justified has haunted me since Monday,” said Roberson.

Roberson and Williams said they will not stop pushing for justice.

“We’re going to petition the Department of Justice to open an investigation to make sure that we get justice for this baby. It just won’t end here,” said Turner.

Turner and Crump said the videos from MBI match the results of their independent autopsy.

Kohen was shot through the side, right to left. According to Crump, MBI said a total of three bullets were fired.

“The third bullet from the side, the bullet that killed one-year-old baby Kohen Wiley, was not justified,” said Crump.

After being cleared by the Mississippi Attorney General, Senatobia Police Officer Hunter Foster reportedly resigned, according to Turner.

Kohen’s family, Crump’s team, and the community said they want Foster decertified.

“It’s not a white or Black issue. It’s a right or wrong issue,” said Brackin Camp. “This was way too much force; it’s unbelievable what happened in the Walmart parking lot that day.”

A special meeting was called by the Senatobia Board of Aldermen and the Mayor on Wednesday. WMC news crews were there; however, a motion was passed to turn the meeting into a closed executive session regarding police personnel.

Nugent family rift and 'proxy' theory probed by police after alleged attack on MP Helen Haines

Victoria Police are investigating a potential rift between Brendan Nugent and his family.

Actual Article Body:
By KYLIE STEVENS, SENIOR BREAKING NEWS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  11:29 AEDT, 23 October 2026   |  Updated:  11:35 AEDT, 23 October 2026

A possible rift between the man accused of deliberately hitting independent MP Helen Haines with a car and his family is a line of inquiry being examined by officers, according to Victoria Police.

Brendan Nugent, 43, was arrested in Wangaratta on Monday afternoon after Haines, 65, suffered severe lower-body injuries when she was allegedly struck by a Toyota LandCruiser vehicle multiple times.

The federal MP for Indi remains in a critical but stable condition after both of her legs were amputated.

Nugent was charged late Tuesday with multiple offences including dangerous driving causing serious harm. He has not applied for bail and remains in custody.

On Friday, Victoria Police Commissioner Mike Bush confirmed officers were investigating a potential rift between Nugent and his family as part of their inquiries.

He was asked by ABC Mildura whether police were investigating the possibility that Nugent's alleged attack on Haines was a 'proxy' for grievances involving his family.

'Yes, it is,' he said.

'It sounds like a cliché, but every line of inquiry is open... Every action is under review.'

Commissioner Bush said Nugent's father, Rod, and the father's partner Christine Cunningham, had been 'very, very helpful' to the police investigation.

More to come.

Victoria Police are investigating a potential rift between Brendan Nugent and his family after he was charged over the alleged attack on MP Helen Haines
